messages:
omar: quick share — ran a batch of perf probes comparing streaming chat vs non-streaming completions with different mb sizes, found some odd tail behavior
maria: nice, what configs? model, seq, hw
omar: model: rw-open-7b, seq=1024 typical, GPU A100 80GB, kernels: auto-selection enabled, kv cache on, tests against 10k short interactive sessions
jin: high level result pls
omar: p50 ~ same across mb=1/2/8, p95 best at mb=2 for streaming, p99 spikes at mb>=8 for chat streaming :thinking:
kevin: non-streaming completions behaved differently?
omar: yeah, for non-streaming completions we could push mb=8/16 with throughput gains and MUCH lower p99 vs chat at same mb
maria: hypothesis: streaming introduces tail work (small incremental decoding + flushes) that interacts poorly with kernel switch + kv warmup
jin: did you capture kernel switch logs? I bet fused-attn fallback shows up when effective seq*mb crosses threshold
omar: pasted small trace snippet:
```
[2025-02-12T14:22:11Z] choose_kernel: fused_attn -> default (reason: seq_eff 2048 > fusion_threshold)
[2025-02-12T14:22:11Z] kv_cache: miss_rate 0.12, warmup_latency +9ms
[2025-02-12T14:22:11Z] mb_size=8 -> queue_wait +6ms
```
kevin: that + queue wait explains p99 jumps
maria: did you try forcing kernel hinting to prefer fused_attn even when seq_eff high? or lowering fusion threshold temporarily
omar: forced fused_attn gives p99 drop ~8-12ms for chat at mb=8 but increases p50 by 3-4ms and causes GPU mem pressure on jumbo prompts
jin: so tradeoff is clear — kernel selection acts like a step function, microbatch sizing moves us across it, streaming chat has shorter per-request work but more KV churn -> tail
maria: any KV cache mitigation? prewarming, pinned kv shards, or stronger prefix caching?
omar: prewarming per-client helps: reducing initial kv miss from 12% -> 2% shaved ~6ms off p99; but prewarm adds cost for many cold clients
kevin: for non-streaming completions, batching amortizes kv warmup across tokens, so mb>=8 wins
jin: action items?
maria: 1) add a small kernel-hint override knob per-deployment so SREs can bias toward fused paths for chat-heavy traffic
maria: 2) evaluate an adaptive mb policy: streaming sessions default mb=2, escalate to mb=8 after kv warmup and after N tokens
omar: 3) add a perf metric: kernel_switch_count and kv_miss_ratio per-route -> helps correlate with tail incidents
kevin: 4) perf-bot: add alert rule for p99 delta > 10ms correlated with kernel_switch_count > 5/min
perf-bot: noted. Alert template created: "p99_regression_with_kernel_switch" -> channel eng-runtime
jin: can we simulate multi-tenant mix? experiments so far are single-tenant load
omar: yes I’ll run mixed traffic sweep tomorrow (chat 60% / completions 40%) and try adaptive mb policy emulation
maria: thanks — if the mixed sim shows the adaptive policy keeps p99 within SLO we can ship a conservative rollout
kevin: also document cost tradeoffs — fused_attn hints might use more GPU cycles, need cost-per-token delta
omar: logging results to Metrics board, will drop the summary CSV here when done :eyes:
